analysis.title: Global Macro Chart of the Day (#198): US wealth effects over time
key_insights: UBS says the US equity market is increasingly a driver of its macro forecasts rather than only an outcome. It now often starts by asking how equities would react to a shock (oil spike, tariffs, AI disappointment), because that reaction alone can swing consumption.
US holdings of equities and mutual funds are close to 200% of GDP, up from 108% just before the dot-com bust. Pension entitlements add another 110% of GDP and are excluded from that figure.
A 10% move in the equity market shifts household wealth by about 20% of GDP, so even a small propensity to consume out of wealth adds up.
UBS assumes a marginal propensity to consume of 6% for real estate (literature range 2-9% by horizon) and 3% for equities (a classic survey gives 2-5%, a recent American Economic Review study 3.2%).

Wealth effects depend on who holds the wealth. People lower in the income distribution spend far more of their gains. The coefficients also shift with the estate tax, the move into 401(k)s (long-term savings are less likely to be spent) and the changing mix of wealth.
Excluding the pandemic swings, the 4-quarter wealth effect on consumption is the largest since before the GFC.

The source of the wealth effect has shifted from housing to equities. Housing wealth rose by nearly 70% of GDP over nine years before the GFC. Equity and mutual fund holdings have risen by about the same amount since Q1 2023 alone.
The equity wealth effect is 0.9pp of GDP over the last four quarters. That is nearly 3x its 10-year pre-pandemic average and twice its level just before the dot-com bust.

macro_indicators.interpretation: This is UBS's own calculation from Fed wealth data and assumed spending propensities, not an official statistic. It is nearly 3x the 10-year pre-pandemic average and twice the pre-dot-com-bust level, so consumption is more exposed to equity moves.

macro_indicators.indicator: US household equity and mutual fund holdings
macro_indicators.interpretation: A 10% market move shifts household wealth by about 20% of GDP.

risk_factors: An equity drawdown triggered by an oil spike, tariffs or AI disappointment would reduce consumption through the wealth effect.
The spending propensities are uncertain and shift over time with the estate tax, the move into 401(k)s and the changing mix of wealth.
Equity wealth is concentrated among higher-income households, who spend a smaller share of gains than lower-income households.
charts_described: Figure 1 plots contributions to potential consumption, in GDP percentage points, from real estate, consumer durables, equities, DB pensions, DC pensions, businesses and other assets, with a total wealth effect line, 1990 to 2026. The text states the equity contribution is 0.9pp over the last four quarters and the wealth effect is the largest since before the GFC, excluding the pandemic.
